methods.label: Hypotenuse midpoint and an equilateral triangle
methods.explanation:
Let \(M\) be the midpoint of hypotenuse \(AB\). The right-triangle median property makes \(CM\) equal to the known length \(AC\):
\[
AM=CM=\frac{AB}{2}=3=AC.
\]
Thus \(\triangle AMC\) is equilateral, so \(\angle CAM=60^\circ\). Since \(M\) lies on segment \(AB\), \(\angle A=\angle CAM=60^\circ\).
